rationales: Margulis and Schwartz later developed a five-kingdom classification, but Whittaker introduced the system.
Robert Whittaker introduced the Five Kingdom System in 1969.
John Ray contributed to plant classification but did not introduce this system.
Ernst Haeckel proposed an earlier kingdom classification, not the Five Kingdom System.
Telophase reverses many events of prophase as chromosomes decondense and the nuclear envelope reforms.
Metaphase is the stage when chromosomes align at the cell equator, not the stage telophase reverses.
Anaphase separates chromatids toward opposite poles and is not the usual answer for the reversal of telophase.
Anaphase I is a meiotic stage and is not the stage reversed by telophase.
Prokaryotic chromosomes are generally described as DNA without the histone proteins found in eukaryotic chromosomes.
The prokaryotic chromosome is typically a DNA molecule, so this is the correct choice.
Protein alone cannot make up a chromosome because it carries genetic information in DNA.
Lipids are not the genetic material of a prokaryotic chromosome.
A theory may help explain a law, but it does not keep suggesting new laws in this context.
A deduction is an inference drawn from premises, not what a productive theory keeps suggesting.
Observations may provide evidence for a theory, but they are not the intended answer.
A productive theory can suggest new hypotheses for further testing.
Oscar Hertwig is credited with discovering meiosis.
Golgi is associated with the discovery of the Golgi apparatus, not meiosis.
John Ray was a naturalist and taxonomist, not the discoverer of meiosis.
Walther Flemming described mitosis, not the discovery of meiosis.
The Greek root does not mean smaller.
Metabolism derives from a Greek word meaning change.
Growth is not the meaning of the Greek root of metabolism.
Energy is involved in metabolism but is not the word’s meaning.
The endodermis surrounds the vascular cylinder but is farther out than the pericycle.
The pericycle is the narrow cell layer immediately outside the conducting tissues.
The cortex lies outside the endodermis and is not immediately outside the conducting tissues.
The epidermis is the outermost layer, not the layer next to the conducting tissues.
Mitochondria are not primarily lipid-storage structures.
Protein synthesis mainly occurs at ribosomes, though mitochondria contain some of their own ribosomes.
Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, not mitochondria.
Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration and generate much of the cell’s ATP.
ATP was not first discovered in 1939.
ATP was not first discovered in 1941.
ATP was not first discovered in 1949.
ATP was discovered in 1929 by Karl Lohmann.
Plants are organisms, so the organism level is present and defined.
Plant organs such as roots and leaves are recognizable, so the organ level is defined.
The organ-system level is less clearly defined in plants than in animals.
Plant tissues are identifiable, so the tissue level is defined.
Interphase occupies at least about 90% of the cell cycle.
Karyokinesis is a shorter part of the cell cycle than interphase.
Cytokinesis is a comparatively brief stage of cell division.
Prophase is only one stage of mitosis and does not last for most of the cycle.
E. Chatton first suggested the terms prokaryotic and eukaryotic.
Robert Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom System, not these terms.
Ernst Haeckel proposed an earlier kingdom classification, not these terms.
Margulis contributed to later classification work, but did not first suggest these terms.
These foods are not listed here chiefly as sources of vitamin A.
Although beef liver contains several B vitamins, this combination is intended as a source of vitamin C.
Citrus fruits and green vegetables are characteristic sources of vitamin C, and beef liver also contains it.
These foods are not chiefly identified as sources of vitamin D.
Spindles do not form during telophase; they disassemble.
Spindle formation begins during prophase.
By metaphase, the spindle is already formed and the chromosomes are aligned.
Anaphase involves chromosome separation by the spindle, which formed earlier.
A cubic millimeter of male blood typically contains about 5–5.5 million red blood cells.
The range 4–4.5 million is below the typical male count given here.
The range 6–6.5 million is above the typical male count given here.
The range 7–7.5 million is far above the typical male count given here.
